Website signals

Your three grades — relevance, distance, prominence

Google ranks local results on those three things. Here’s where BrightStar stands on each.

1

Build one real Waltham page

Why: right now Waltham appears once on the site, 7th in a list of served towns. A page that is Waltham-first — Waltham neighbourhoods, landmarks, families — tells Google this is a Waltham business. One strong page for the town you actually want to win beats a 13-town list that dilutes all of them.

What it buys

Relevance — a Waltham-first page of your own

2

Complete the Google profile: services, description, Q&A

Why: in the signed-out view, none of the top 5 shows a description, services list, or Q&A. Nobody above BrightStar has claimed this ground. A Waltham-specific description and a real services list is free relevance that VSM, Havenly, and Gold Star have all left on the table.

What it buys

Relevance +6 · ground none of the top 5 holds

3

Reply to every review — you reply to most, not all

Why: checked Nov 9, BrightStar replied to 4 of its newest 5 reviews — Havenly, at #3, replies to all of theirs. That one unanswered review is the measured gap. (Posting is not the gap: BrightStar already had the freshest post in the top 5, 4 hours old at check time, so no post fix is listed.)

What it buys

Prominence — matches the top 5’s best reply record

Your Agency

Your weekly note

Miriam’s week

Monday 29 September – Sunday 5 October

Miriam came back three times this week, and almost everything she did was built around cards.

What Miriam is working towards

To walk with more ease. That is how she put it herself when she started, and it is what most of her week is chosen around.

Where the work went

Moving and reaching took the biggest share of her week — standing up, stepping out, reaching overhead. Steadiness came next: balance work on her feet, a little at a time. Thinking and focus filled the rest, through the card games and the counting, which she takes to easily.

A moment from the week

On Tuesday afternoon Miriam did six minutes back to back — six separate sessions in under an hour, on her very first day with us.

What is next

More of the same. Short, often, and built around the things she already enjoys.

Win over new inquiries

In plenty of regions, families expect home care to be covered by the government, so private care sounds like an extra they should not have to pay for. Stride changes that conversation: you can show a family exactly how you are helping their loved one achieve their goals, and the strain that lifts off the family itself.
